sources: Thu Aug 27 2026 run, executed 06:12 UTC / 02:12 ET - BEFORE today's 8:30 ET jobless claims and BEFORE the US cash open, so the last complete session on the board is Wednesday Aug 26. THEME: the crude unwind extended to a fourth session while the front end sold off - the curve is flattening from the SHORT end now, which is the opposite of last week's story. CRUDE, FOURTH DOWN SESSION: Brent 87.11 (TradingEconomics Aug 27 print, -0.84% d/d; Aug 26 close 87.84, live quote 87.20), DOWN from 92.17 Monday and ~94 a week ago. Note wide venue dispersion this week - TE's CFD series printed 'just below 89' and 'toward 86' on the SAME Wednesday session, so treat any single Brent number as a range, not a settlement. WTI 81.53. The driver is diplomatic, not physical: Iran and Oman reached an agreement on each country's share of Hormuz waters and related revenues, Trump said 10mb/d passed the strait Tuesday and repeated that mines had been cleared, and last week's US sanctions package spared Iran's trading partners. Tehran cautioned that reopening Hormuz needs more than an Oman deal. Offsetting: Putin reportedly planning escalation in Ukraine; EIA showed US crude stocks flat but gasoline and diesel stocks at seasonal lows. Heating oil 4.21 (-1.19%) - the downstream tightness flagged last run has NOT resolved. VOL: VIX 15.21 Aug 26 close (-1.55% d/d), still near 2026 lows but UP from ~14.25 a week ago. The move came from the 2Y RISING to 4.23% (+1bp d/d, but -6bp on the month) while the 10Y stalled after Tuesday's ~10bp rally on cheaper oil and Bessent's doubled 4bn buyback programme.
